facts.statement: The genus Yixianornis was described by Zhou and Zhang in 2001.
Fossils of Yixianornis were found in the Jiufotang Formation near Chaoyang, China, dating to the early Aptian age approximately 120 million years ago.
facts.quote: Its remains have been found in the Jiufotang Formation at Chaoyang (People's Republic of China) dated to the early Aptian age, around 120 million years ago.

facts.statement: The species name grabaui honors American paleontologist Amadeus William Grabau.
facts.quote: The specific name, grabaui, is named after American paleontologist Amadeus William Grabau, who surveyed China in the early 20th century.

facts.statement: The single known specimen is nearly complete with mostly uncrushed bones that were not split during slab separation.
facts.quote: It is nearly complete and, unlike many other fossils, the bones are mostly uncrushed and were not split in half when the stone slabs were initially separated.

facts.statement: This specimen is one of the few Mesozoic ornithurans preserving clear impressions of wing and tail feathers.
facts.quote: It is also one of the few known Mesozoic ornithuran bird specimens that preserve clear impressions of the wing and tail feathers.

facts.statement: Yixianornis was about the size of a chicken.
facts.quote: Yixianornis was moderately sized compared to other yanornithiformes, at about the size of a chicken.

facts.statement: The specimen measured 19 to 20 cm in length, 11.5 cm in height at the hips, and had a wingspan of about 40 cm.
facts.quote: IVPP V12631 was measured approximately 19 to 20 cm long (excluding feathers), 11.5 cm tall at the hips, with a wingspan of about 40 cm.

facts.statement: The estimated body weight of Yixianornis was between 200 and 350 grams.
facts.quote: Its body weight has been estimated to have been 200 to 350 g.

facts.statement: While Yixianornis had small peg-like teeth, the jaw tips were toothless and pockmarked with pits and grooves, possibly indicating a beak.
facts.quote: All three had teeth, though in Yixianornis the tips of the jaws were toothless and pockmarked with small pits and grooves, possibly indicating the presence of a beak.

facts.statement: The breastbone had a strong keel for flight muscles and a unique fenestra found in yanornithiformes.
facts.quote: The breastbone bore a strong keel for the attachment of flight muscles, and contained a distinct opening or fenestra, a unique characteristic of yanornithiformes.

facts.statement: The fossil shows a backward-pointing hallux, but lacks clear evidence of the bone twist required for a permanently reversed toe.
facts.quote: The hallux, or reversed, perching toe of modern birds, is noticeably pointed backward in the fossil. However, there is no clear evidence that the bone itself was twisted, which would indicate that the toe was permanently reversed.

facts.statement: Each wing had about five primary feathers, with the longest measuring approximately 6.7 cm.
facts.quote: There were about five primary feathers on each wing, the longest measuring about 6.7 cm.

facts.statement: Carbonized tissue impressions reveal a rectrical bulb that allowed the tail feathers to fan out during flight and retract at rest.
facts.quote: Additionally, carbonized tissue impressions show that it had a rectrical bulb, the muscles around the tail which allow the tail feathers to be fanned out during flight, and retraced when at rest.

facts.statement: A 2006 study suggests Yixianornis likely preferred dense vegetation environments due to its ability to fan its tail and broad wings for high maneuverability.
facts.quote: In a 2006 study, Julia Clarke, Zhou Zhonghe and Fucheng Zhang found that the ability to fan the tail, along with the broad wings, show that it probably preferred environments with dense vegetation, where high maneuverability in flight would be necessary.

facts.statement: Yixianornis belongs to the parent group Hongshanornithidae.
The time range for Yixianornis is the Aptian stage, from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

rejected.quote: There were eight tail feathers, up to 9.2 cm long, anchored to a pygostyle and rectrical bulb (see below) as in modern birds.

rejected.quote: Comparisons between the scleral rings of Yixianornis and modern birds and reptiles indicate that it may have been diurnal, similar to most modern birds.
